hypothesis: A text encoder applied to entire table records made unstable gains. A more precise role is to find when the value of a selector field refers to one of several comparable documented input fields. This can supply the value of the referenced field directly to a classifier. Task1's released README explicitly declares the ordered feature headers; earlier anonymous-row experiments suppressed these headers.
resources: Only confirmed feature names in the original ordinary solver's task spec, ordinal fit-row arrays, and the pinned offline BGE encoder. Never hardcode a field name, entity, dataset, category value or label-to-field mapping. The algorithm searches shared-vocabulary field families and other categorical fields. A winning match must distinguish at least two fields, cover 60 percent of fitting rows and have an absolute resemblance and relative margin. Anonymous or ambiguous headings can lead to abstention.
candidates: Fit one global recurring-context CatBoost on its old features plus the selected value, selector-value token, parsed quantity and relative quantity from documented binding. Optionally train local depth-four 400-round trees for the up to eight largest supported selector values each with at least 192 fitting rows and both classes. Share the global model and use n/(n+500) shrinkage when blending local predictions. One plus at most eight real fits. Scope and thresholds are frozen before predictions.
decision: Use the established 4061 fitting rows. Seal the global and partially pooled predictions for all three development panels before comparing shares to the existing research reference on 808 nomination rows. Lock a share then test on 817 and 807 rows, with no decrease on either and pooled gain at least .003 to earn an ordinary-entry test. If the candidate proceeds, controls receive the same documented feature names. Test anonymous headings and column permutation before ordinary integration. No course validation, final test, language model API or external task data.
